programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha Daolag-bhreac is Seillean air an dòigh glan nuair tha na duilleagan a’ cuachail gu talamh! Daolag-bhreac and Seillean are delighted when the leaves start twirling to the ground!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Marvin, Oona and Silky are playing hide-and-seek in the Underwater Cave. Silky tries lots of different hiding places but feels frustrated when Oona and Marvin find her easily. When it's her turn to look for her friends, Silky is too slow on land and is disappointed when she can't find her friends. But when she agrees to play once more, Silky finds a hiding place that's just right for her! Tha Marvin, Oona is Silky a' cluich Falach-fead san Uamh Fo-uisg'. Tha Silky a' feuchainn tòrr dhiofair àitichean falaich, ach tha i air a ruigheachd nuair a lorgas Oona is Marvin i gun strì. Nuair a thig an t-àm dhì-se a' caraidean a lorg, tha Silky ro mhall air tìr, 's tha i tàmailteach nuair nach lorg i a caraidean. Ach le aont' cluich aon trup eile, tha Silky ri lorg àite-falaich a tha fèir ceart dhìth-se!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: It's a hot day on Puffin Rock, and Oona, May and Marvin want to swim in the pond but find the water has dried up, meaning no swimming today! Even the frogs are gone... all but one, and he's hopping away. Where is he going? The friends hop along to find out - follow the frog sounds like a fun game! The frog leads them all over the island, but will they be able to keep up with him and find his friends? Latha teth a th' ann air Creag Nam Buthaidean, 's tha Oona, May is Marvin 'son snàmh san loch, ach tha an loch air tiormachadh... 's le sin cha bhi snàmh ann an-diugh. Tha fiù 's gach losgann air teicheadh... gach fear ach aon, 's tha esan ri leum air falbh. Cà' bheil e a' dol? Tha na caraidean a' leum 'son fuasgladh fhaighinn air a' chùis... Deagh gheam' a th' ann an Lean an Losgann! An losgann gan toirt air feadh an eilein.'N tèid ac' air cumail ris an losgann, agus a charaidean a lorg?

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha Boban ag iarraidh Fuigheag a thoirt air chuairt – mar chù beag! Ach chan eil cùisean ag obrachadh a-mach cho sìmplidh 's a shaoileadh tu! Cò tha toirt cò airson cuairt? Boban is going to take Fuigheag for a walk, like a little dog! But things don’t work out as simply as you’d expect! Who is taking who for a walk?

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid a’ còcaireachd cuide ri a caraidean. An-diugh tha Hannah agus Matthew cuide rithe agus iad a’ dèanamh nudailean steigeach le feòil-circe agus mil. Ach mus tòisich iad, feumaidh iad a bhith cinnteach gu bheil an stuth tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, bidh iad a’ dèanamh liosta agus a’ dol dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach cò às a tha mil a’ tighinn. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson na nudailean a dhèanamh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd gan ithe! Linda Macleod and friends cook a number of tasty dishes. In this episode, Linda is joined by Hannah and Matthew to make sticky noodles with chicken. But before they start, they have to ensure they have all the ingredients and, if not, they make a list and go shopping. They also learn more about where honey comes from. Then it’s back into the kitchen to make the noodles before sitting down at the table to eat them!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Ailig Dòmhnallach a’ leughadh Sligeanach Fànais. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Ross Montgomery agus a dhealbhachadh le David Litchfield. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Alec MacDonald reads Sligeanach Fànais, written by Ross Montgomery, illustrated by David Litchfield and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair tha Partaidh nam Fiaclairean dol a thachairt, the Mrs Oh 'g iarraidh buidealair. Ach chan eil Mgr P deònach taic a thoirt seachad. Dè nì Stella is an Teaghlach Rìoghail airson cuideachadh leis a’ chuirm? When the Dentist Party is about to take place, Mrs Oh would like a butler. But Mr P isn’t prepared to help out. What will Stella and the Royal Family do to help at the event?

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Tha Stella air a glacadh eadar Mia is Freya nuair a tha ‘ad ag argamaid. Ciamar a gheibh i fuasgladh air an trod gus am bi ‘ad air ais nan caraidean a-rithist Stella is caught between Mia and Freya when they argue. How will she find a solution to the fighting so that they will be friends again?

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha Seonaidh sgìth de bhith na chàraid Ghumbail is the e son dearbhadh g’ eil e cheart cho comasach leis fhèin. An dùil ciamar a thèid dha leis a sin? Seonaidh is tired of being a Gumbail twin and he wants to prove that he’s just as capable on his own. How will he get on with that?

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Tha Fionn feumach air taic bho na Neachdan. Feumar athair, Tormod Mòr, a stad mus faigh e greim air ulaidh sònraichte. Chan eil Fionn 'son ‘s gum boin athair dhan ulaidh 's gum bi e air a ghortachadh ri linn sin. Saoil ciamar a thèid leotha? Fionn needs help from the Neachdan. His father, Tormod Mòr, must be stopped from getting his hands on a treasure. Fionn doesn’t want his father to touch this treasure and get hurt in the process. How will they get on with this?

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc: Kate Macleod, The Hebridean Mermaid, takes us on a journey to some of the hidden gems of the Hebrides.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Tha Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na ciad ceumannan gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Coinnichidh sinn ris an neach-ionnsachaidh Sophie Day às an Eaglais Bhreac, agus tha Calum MacIlleathain a’ lorg ìomhaigh ann an uamh air Eilean Dà Bharra far Maol Chinn Tìre. Joy Dunlop continues to guide us through the first basic steps to speak Gaelic. We meet learner Sophie Day from Falkirk, and Calum Maclean keeps a keen eye on the tide whilst on the hunt for spectacular cave art on Davaar Island in the Mull of Kintyre.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: Murdina is thrown into turmoil when she realises that Johan is becoming a majority shareholder in the mill. Manager Sìleas offers newcomer Rory a job as one of the drivers. But just who exactly is this mysterious Irish stranger, Rory? Ivor and Dòmhnall’s relationship is put to the test when Ivor shares his fears that he may be responsible for the fire. Tha Murdina troimhe-chèile nuair a tha i ag ionnsachadh gur ann aig Johan a bhios an roinn as motha ‘sa mhuileann. Tha Sìleas, ceannard na muilne, a’ toirt obair do Rory mar dhraibhear, ‘s e air ùr nochdadh. Ach cò dìreach a th’ anns a’ choigreach Èireannach, Rory? Tha buaireadh eadar Ivor is Dòmhnall, le Ivor ag aideachadh gur dòcha gur esan as coireach airson an teine. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Aithris le Shona NicEanraig bho 2006, a’ rannsachadh mar a tha boireannaich gan cùiltearachd à Moldòbha gu taobh an iar na Roinn Eòrpa – cuid dhiubh a Bhreatainn Shona Henderson’s 2006 report investigating the trafficking of women from Moldova to western Europe, many of whom end up in the United Kingdom. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Alba fon Talamh/Scotland Underground
programme.desc: Calum explores the underground sites of central Scotland. First, author Mairi Kidd introduces him to a lesser known history of Edinburgh below the city streets. Then he ventures under the busy platforms of Glasgow Central Station, where Calum discovers an atmospheric disused Victorian platform. In Dunoon, Calum gets help from his friend Kenny Rankin to access the Paper Caves and find out more about a story that dates back almost 350 years, connecting the Campbell clan with the site. ’S a’ phrògram mu dheireadh, nì Calum rannsachadh air làraich fon talamh ann am meadhan na h-Alba. Innsidh an t-ùghdair, Màiri Kidd, dha mun eachdraidh fo shràidean Dhùn Èideann air nach eil mòran eòlach. Fo àrd-ùrlairean trang Stèisean Rèile Meadhan Ghlaschu, gheibh Calum lorg air àrd-ùrlar iongantach, neo-chleachte bho linn Bhictòiria. Ann an Dùn Omhain, bheir a charaid, Coinneach MacFhraing, cuideachadh do Chalum gus Uamhan nam Pàipear a ruighinn agus tuilleadh ionnsachadh mu sgeulachd bhon t-seachdamh linn deug a tha a’ ceangal na Caimbeulaich ris an t-sreath uamhan seo. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke head to the woods in search of birch sap, fungi and midgies!

programme.title: Caileag nan Eun
programme.desc: Tha Caitlin na boireannach òg a th’air a beò-ghlacadh le bhith a’ coimhead air eòin. Nuair a smaoineachas sinn air a’ chur-seachad seo is mathaid nach e òigridh a’ chiad fheadhainn a thig a-steach oirnn - ach tha Caitlin airson seo atharrachadh. Mar sin, tha i a’ falbh air turas mòr mun cuairt Alba, a shireadh daoine òga aig a bheil an aon ùidh rithe fhèin. Anns a’ phrògram seo cluinnear na sgeulachdan pearsanta acasan mu na buannachdan agus mun mhòr-thlachd a tha iad a’ faighinn às a’ chur-seachad iongantach seo. Caitlin is an avid birdwatcher, but as a young female, she goes against stereotype. Keen to connect with people who share her passion, she sets off on a road trip around Scotland to meet other birders who are defying the typecasts and to uncover some of the personal stories behind the hobby. Together, they share the joys and frustrations of birdwatching as well as the pure exhilaration in spotting a bird that means so much to them. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Air sgàth mar a tha trioblaidean slàinte air a bhith aig Ruairidh agus a chridhe a’ fàiligeadh, feumaidh e a bhith mothachail mu na tha e ag ithe. Tha Ùisdean air aontachadh taic a thoirt dhà agus tha iad a’ cruthachadh reasabaidhean far a bheilear a’ seachnadh salann is siùcar, ach aig a’ cheann thall – chan eil ionndrainn orra! Tha reasabaidhean airson Giomach le Sabhs Jerk, Anann air a Ghriligeadh le Sabhs Ruma Charamail, Bonnach-èisg Criospach agus Tart Bakewell Dearcan is Àmoin uile air an atharrachadh gus biadh blasta is fallain a chruthachadh do Ruairidh. Part of Roddy’s health scare with heart failure means he has to adjust what he eats. Uisdean has agreed to help him out as they come up with some recipes where neither salt nor sugar is used, and in the end neither ingredient is missed! Lobster in jerk sauce, grilled pineapple with rum caramel sauce, crispy fishcake and berry almond Bakewell tart recipes are all tweaked to provide Roddy with tasty and healthy meals. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: A Wild Year
programme.desc: In the north east of England lies a wild and remote moorland - 550 square miles of windswept heather-clad uplands and deep, sheltered valleys or dales. These are the North York Moors. Over millennia, this spectacular landscape has been shaped by the elements - by water and ice - and more recently by people. Remote farmsteads are dotted all across the high country. On Dale Head Farm, the Barraclough family raise tough Swaledale and Cheviot sheep, animals bred for the moorland life. They can be left out on the hill year-round because over many generations they have built up an intimate knowledge of their patch - each flock is ‘hefted’ to the land. The flocks are brought down off the moors to the shelter of the dales a couple of times each year - in the spring for lambing and again in the summer to be shorn of their heavy winter coats. The best shearers can clip 300 sheep in a day.

programme.title: India: Nature's Wonderland
programme.desc: Wildlife expert Liz Bonnin, actor Freida Pinto and mountaineer Jon Gupta reveal the hidden wonders of India's surprising natural world. This is a land where the tea comes with added elephants, gibbons sing to greet the morning, tigers dance and lions roam.

programme.title: Art of Scandinavia
programme.desc: In episode two of Andrew Graham-Dixon's epic journey through Scandinavian art and landscape, Denmark emerges from modest beginnings to become one of the greatest powers and arbiters of taste in northern Europe - a story of incredible transformation befitting the homeland of the great fairytale spinner Hans Christian Andersen, creator of The Ugly Duckling and The Emperor's New Clothes.

programme.title: Gluck: Who Did She Think He Was?
programme.desc: The untold story of Britain's cross-dressing high society painter. Gluck was one of the British Establishment's go-to portrait painters of the 1930s. Her shows were attended by royalty, aristocrats and celebrities. She also dressed as a man and called her exhibitions 'one-man shows'. Her lovers were all women, including flower arranger to the stars Constance Spry, and Edith Heald, the ex-mistress of WB Yeats. How did Gluck get away with it? This programme is available to mark the inaugural Jewish Culture Month.

programme.title: An Art Lovers' Guide
programme.desc: In the final episode of the series, our intrepid cultural explorers Janina Ramirez and Alastair Sooke set off on their most adventurous trip yet - to Baku, capital of Azerbaijan.

programme.title: Art That Made Us
programme.desc: The world wars force artists to grapple with destruction and savagery, challenging conventions and the old imperial order, while those fleeing war bring new ideas to Britain.

On Dale Head Farm, the Barraclough family raise tough Swaledale and Cheviot sheep, animals bred for the moorland life. They can be left out on the hill year-round because over many generations they have built up an intimate knowledge of their patch - each flock is ‘hefted’ to the land. The flocks are brought down off the moors to the shelter of the dales a couple of times each year - in the spring for lambing and again in the summer to be shorn of their heavy winter coats. The best shearers can clip 300 sheep in a day.

programme.title: University Challenge

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take you so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. It is all about making connections between things which may appear, at first glance, not to be connected at all.

programme.title: India: Nature's Wonderland
programme.desc: Wildlife expert Liz Bonnin, actor Freida Pinto and mountaineer Jon Gupta reveal the hidden wonders of India's surprising natural world. This is a land where the tea comes with added elephants, gibbons sing to greet the morning, tigers dance and lions roam.

programme.title: Art of Scandinavia
programme.desc: In episode two of Andrew Graham-Dixon's epic journey through Scandinavian art and landscape, Denmark emerges from modest beginnings to become one of the greatest powers and arbiters of taste in northern Europe - a story of incredible transformation befitting the homeland of the great fairytale spinner Hans Christian Andersen, creator of The Ugly Duckling and The Emperor's New Clothes.

programme.title: Gluck: Who Did She Think He Was?
programme.desc: The untold story of Britain's cross-dressing high society painter. Gluck was one of the British Establishment's go-to portrait painters of the 1930s. Her shows were attended by royalty, aristocrats and celebrities. She also dressed as a man and called her exhibitions 'one-man shows'. Her lovers were all women, including flower arranger to the stars Constance Spry, and Edith Heald, the ex-mistress of WB Yeats. How did Gluck get away with it? This programme is available to mark the inaugural Jewish Culture Month.

programme.title: An Art Lovers' Guide

programme.title: Art That Made Us
programme.desc: The world wars force artists to grapple with destruction and savagery, challenging conventions and the old imperial order, while those fleeing war bring new ideas to Britain.

programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Carol, Sam, Ben and Josie – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Crazy Rich Asians
programme.desc: New Yorker Rachel Chu accompanies her longtime boyfriend, Nick Young, to his best friend's wedding in Singapore. Excited about visiting Asia for the first time but nervous about meeting Nick's family, Rachel is unprepared to learn that Nick has neglected to mention a few key details about his life. Not only is he the scion of one of the country's wealthiest families, but also one of its most sought-after bachelors. Being on Nick's arm puts a target on Rachel's back, with jealous socialites and, worse, Nick's own disapproving mother taking aim. It soon becomes clear that the only thing crazier than love is family.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate why some brands continue to label their wet wipes as flushable despite the major drain blockages caused by wet wipes that cost millions to repair every year. One woman whose garden was flooded with sewage thanks to such a blockage says enough is enough. At the advice clinic in South Shields, the team meet the wheelchair user let down by a travel company that promised an accessible coach holiday. And in his latest how-to guide, consumer expert Harry Kind explains all you need to do to appeal against a parking ticket.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Carol, Sam, Ben and Josie – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: The Smuggling Business: Undercover
programme.desc: Over the past two years, tens of thousands of migrants have crossed the English Channel in small boats from northern France, despite repeated promises by successive governments to stop the trade. This undercover BBC investigation reveals how people smuggling gangs are operating in plain sight inside a migrant camp in Dunkirk. It exposes a highly organised criminal marketplace driven by fierce competition between rival groups, who enforce control over the settlements through fear, violence and intimidation. The film examines efforts by UK authorities to disrupt and dismantle the criminal networks profiting from the crossings, and questions whether those measures are keeping pace with the scale and sophistication of the operation. BBC investigative reporter Josie Hannett also travels to Crowborough, where opposition to a new asylum seeker accommodation site has turned the town into a flashpoint in the national immigration debate. She asks whether current government policy is likely to deter future arrivals, or whether the UK is preparing for a future that will require many more such sites across the south east

programme.title: The Smuggling Business: Undercover
programme.desc: Over the past two years, tens of thousands of migrants have crossed the English Channel in small boats from northern France, despite repeated promises by successive governments to stop the trade. This undercover BBC investigation reveals how people smuggling gangs are operating in plain sight inside a migrant camp in Dunkirk. It exposes a highly organised criminal marketplace driven by fierce competition between rival groups, who enforce control over the settlements through fear, violence and intimidation. The film examines efforts by UK authorities to disrupt and dismantle the criminal networks profiting from the crossings, and questions whether those measures are keeping pace with the scale and sophistication of the operation. BBC investigative reporter Josie Hannett also travels to Crowborough, where opposition to a new asylum seeker accommodation site has turned the town into a flashpoint in the national immigration debate. She asks whether current government policy is likely to deter future arrivals, or whether the UK is preparing for a future that will require many more such sites across the south east

programme.title: Crazy Rich Asians
programme.desc: New Yorker Rachel Chu accompanies her longtime boyfriend, Nick Young, to his best friend's wedding in Singapore. Excited about visiting Asia for the first time but nervous about meeting Nick's family, Rachel is unprepared to learn that Nick has neglected to mention a few key details about his life. Not only is he the scion of one of the country's wealthiest families, but also one of its most sought-after bachelors. Being on Nick's arm puts a target on Rachel's back, with jealous socialites and, worse, Nick's own disapproving mother taking aim. It soon becomes clear that the only thing crazier than love is family.

programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate why some brands continue to label their wet wipes as flushable despite the major drain blockages caused by wet wipes that cost millions to repair every year. programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Carol, Sam, Ben and Josie – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. programme.title: The Smuggling Business: Undercover
programme.desc: Over the past two years, tens of thousands of migrants have crossed the English Channel in small boats from northern France, despite repeated promises by successive governments to stop the trade. This undercover BBC investigation reveals how people smuggling gangs are operating in plain sight inside a migrant camp in Dunkirk. It exposes a highly organised criminal marketplace driven by fierce competition between rival groups, who enforce control over the settlements through fear, violence and intimidation. The film examines efforts by UK authorities to disrupt and dismantle the criminal networks profiting from the crossings, and questions whether those measures are keeping pace with the scale and sophistication of the operation. BBC investigative reporter Josie Hannett also travels to Crowborough, where opposition to a new asylum seeker accommodation site has turned the town into a flashpoint in the national immigration debate. She asks whether current government policy is likely to deter future arrivals, or whether the UK is preparing for a future that will require many more such sites across the south east

Currently based in the busy Berkshire town of Wokingham, the Paralympic gold medallist rower and his physiotherapist wife have £400,000 to find their perfect family home. Along the way, Denise also catches up with another growing family who have already made their own escape to this beautiful part of the country.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The experts race against time to restore a historic carriage before a town procession, a unique musical instrument needs some TLC, and Will gets a makeover at Scotland’s oldest bespoke tailors.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Carol, Sam, Ben and Josie – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Crazy Rich Asians
programme.desc: New Yorker Rachel Chu accompanies her longtime boyfriend, Nick Young, to his best friend's wedding in Singapore. Excited about visiting Asia for the first time but nervous about meeting Nick's family, Rachel is unprepared to learn that Nick has neglected to mention a few key details about his life. Not only is he the scion of one of the country's wealthiest families, but also one of its most sought-after bachelors. Being on Nick's arm puts a target on Rachel's back, with jealous socialites and, worse, Nick's own disapproving mother taking aim. It soon becomes clear that the only thing crazier than love is family.

programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate why some brands continue to label their wet wipes as flushable despite the major drain blockages caused by wet wipes that cost millions to repair every year. One woman whose garden was flooded with sewage thanks to such a blockage says enough is enough. At the advice clinic in South Shields, the team meet the wheelchair user let down by a travel company that promised an accessible coach holiday. And in his latest how-to guide, consumer expert Harry Kind explains all you need to do to appeal against a parking ticket.

programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Carol, Sam, Ben and Josie – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: The Harbour
programme.desc: Aberdeen Harbour, on the north east coast of Scotland, is one of Britain's oldest businesses and one of Europe's most modern ports. It is the heartbeat of the offshore oil and gas industry. Every year, more than 8,000 boats pass through the harbour waters, helped by the hidden world of the men and women who keep it running 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. This is their story... In this programme, it's Ralph Greig's first day of training. He's being put through a tough test on the simulator ahead of stepping up to being a harbour pilot. Ex-sailor Ellen Haughland has her heart set on stepping into Ralph's shoes as a VTS controller. Can she become Aberdeen's first ever woman in that role? Out at sea, the crew on the Bibby Sapphire are bracing themselves for 'Mother Nature at her worst' as a force ten storm heads directly towards them. Meanwhile, in the Crown & Anchor, barmaid Val Morrison could never have expected to be serving a troop of Morris dancers...

programme.title: The Harbour
programme.desc: Aberdeen Harbour, on the north east coast of Scotland, is one of Britain's oldest businesses and one of Europe's most modern ports. It is the heartbeat of the offshore oil and gas industry. Every year, more than eight thousand boats pass through the harbour waters, helped by the hidden world of the men and women who keep it running 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. This is their story... In this episode, we're up at 4.30am to meet larger than life fish merchant Doug Rennie for his daily drive north to get the best prices at the Peterhead fish auction. He also has the big move to a new state-of-the-art fish processing factory to contend with. While The Highland Prince loads with vital supplies for a North Sea oil rig, on-the-job training for new pilot Ralph Greig serves as a jolting reminder that this is one of the most dangerous jobs in the harbour. And the Harbour chaplain's tireless work to open a Sea Farer's centre in Aberdeen finally pays off, but success is followed by a devastating blow...

programme.title: Only Child
programme.desc: Ken needs to resit his driving exam in order to win back his licence. Richard offers to take him out on a mock test, not realising just how rusty his dad has become behind the wheel.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: After an emotional funeral for his dad, Colin and Cathy have the neighbours round but understandably Colin is not his usual upbeat self. Christine was not impressed with the service or the priest and, as usual, is not backward about coming forward with her opinions on the whole affair. And as Beth, Eric and Ian try to make their excuses to leave early, Cathy manages to foil their escape by inviting more of the neighbours in. As the drink flows with Cathy's encouragement, Colin reminisces about the late departed Willie and encourages his neighbours to do the same. But as the guests look on - brandy glasses in hand - Cathy tries to turn the solemn occasion into a party, complete with wildly inappropriate music and games.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: As spring turns to summer, Dougie is in Cairngorms National Park to find out how authorities are protecting precious habitats from the risk of wildfires. Cammy is on his Ayrshire farm at the peak of lambing season, and Anne ventures to the Isle of May to find out how extreme weather is driving apart one species of birds that mate for life. She also reflects on her own special family connection to the island and pays a visit to the lighthouse where her grandfather was posted. Elsewhere, journalist Rachel Bell follows in the footsteps of the Highland Lady who left her stylish mark in Braemar.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: It's time for some early summer colour as Carole Baxter makes the first of her visits to classic Scottish gardens. She visits Glenarn, which has a fabulous collection of rhododendrons looking their best right now. Back at Beechgrove Garden, George Anderson and Calum Clunie are busy refreshing the grass and gravel plot and planting new varieties. Calum demonstrates how to take cuttings from a fuchsia, and there are some ideas on how to manage your plot if you are unlucky enough to have club root in your vegetable patch. And there are all the usual handy hints.

programme.title: Chloe Ayling: My Unbelievable Kidnapping
programme.desc: Glamour model and kidnapping victim Chloe Ayling continues to look back at her terrifying ordeal orchestrated by Black Death. Now safely under the protection of the Italian authorities, she must give evidence in court against the man who enabled her escape from the international sex-trafficking gang – Lukasz Herba. But as the hearing starts and the evidence is laid out, a different picture begins to emerge of this particular suspect. Dazed from the shock of this discovery, Chloe returns home to the UK, finally free of the spectre of a gang she believed could continue to threaten her life. Whilst now free from one unimaginable ordeal, she’s immediately plunged into another as the Italian courts publicly release details of the case and the ongoing investigation to the world’s press. What she hoped to bury as an embarrassing nightmare soon ignites the interest of the global media. Now they know her name and discover where she lives.

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: Birmingham’s Hockley Social Club has been transformed into our very own comedy club. Taking to the stage are Eli Hart, Farhan Solo, Chloe Reynolds, Will BF and Monica Hsueh in a bid to impress our judges and book their place in the final. Award-winning comedian and writer Sarah Keyworth is here to keep the house in order. The judges are comedian, writer and podcaster Aurie Styla and local Brum stand-up Lindsey Santoro. Head judge Fatiha El-Ghorri completes the trio. It’s not going to be easy for them to pick a winner from the five new comics performing. With only five minutes on stage each, the sets are jam-packed with jokes and cutting-edge material, but only one can go through to the grand final in November at City of Culture 25 Bradford’s Alhambra Theatre.

programme.desc: Stacey Solomon and her team face their biggest challenge yet as craft-loving Sue and retired electrician Wayne try to part with 30 years of possessions.

programme.title: Thailand: The Dark Side of Paradise
programme.desc: After being invited to a bar crawl on Khaosan Road, Zara gets under the skin of Bangkok’s notorious red light district, Soi Cowboy - but filming is swiftly shut down by local bar owners and the police. When Zara meets Mike Yu, a young British expat living a life of luxury in the Thai capital, she realises there is more to the city than meets the eye. Meanwhile, a visit to the Bangkok Immigration Detention Centre exposes how easy it is to get caught on the wrong side of the law in Thailand.

programme.title: Thailand: The Dark Side of Paradise
programme.desc: As she explores more of Thailand, Zara visits Pattaya, where she meets Mac, a British YouTuber lifting the lid on Asia’s sex capital. However, Annie, a local sex worker, reveals the harsh reality of working in the illegal sex industry. After journeying to the island of Ko Phangan, Zara finds her paradise: beautiful beaches and tranquil temples, but Lucio, a Brit who built a burgeoning cannabis business here whilst the drug was decriminalised, reveals that navigating the local law isn’t always easy. Hugo shares his shocking near-death experience that exposes how the island plays by its own rules.

programme.title: Thailand: The Dark Side of Paradise
programme.desc: Zara experiences Ko Phangan’s world-famous Full Moon Party, but beneath the cheap cocktails, music and fire shows, there is danger lurking as the medical team treat a possible drink-spiking victim. Finally, Zara journeys to Phuket, where she meets Dave, an expat who shows off the island’s high-end beach clubs. She also meets Shakira, a tourist in trouble with the Thai police who reveals how easily dream holidays can go wrong. Zara then discovers the tragic case of a British holidaymaker who recently lost their life on the island and whose family is still searching for answers. A final catch-up with backpacker Loukas exposes the true price of letting loose in Thailand.

programme.title: Kidnapped by My Mum
programme.desc: At 11 years old, Alex vanished on holiday with his mother and grandfather for six years. Now, he's retracing his steps across Europe to tell the full story for the first time.

programme.title: Fake Friend: The Ticket Scammer
programme.desc: How a Somerset high-flyer turned his charm and connections into tools of deception – conning his school friends and hundreds of others while living a life of glamour himself.

programme.title: Children of the Blitz
programme.desc: From September 1940 to May 1941, during the Second World War, over 35,000 tonnes of bombs and incendiaries were dropped on towns and cities across the UK during the infamous Luftwaffe aerial bombing campaign that became known as the Blitz. Just before the outbreak of war, the British government’s Operation Pied Piper put plans in place to evacuate millions of children, but only 800,000 left towns and cities that were vulnerable to attack. These are the stories of some of the two million children who stayed at home, often to help their families or because their parents couldn’t bear to send them away. This documentary features some of the last people who witnessed the reality of the Blitz, with their testimony offering an intimate, enlightening and moving portrait of wartime Britain through children’s eyes.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway adventure through Uzbekistan reaches its finale in the historic city of Bukhara. Amidst the medieval Islamic architecture, Michael goes in search of a centuries-old Jewish community. Stepping inside a 420-year-old synagogue and a family home, he’s introduced to unique customs and traditions, and a fragrant green dish that has made Bukharan Jews famous worldwide. Michael grapples with kurash, an ancient form of upright wrestling once used to select the bravest warriors and now also increasingly popular as a sport for young Uzbek women. Michael’s exploration of Uzbekistan culminates in the vast Kyzylkum Desert, where he experiences the life of nomadic tribes who once roamed its vast sandy plains. His Central Asian journey concludes among the horses and riders who brave all to take part in one of the most dangerous equestrian sports in the world.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein lead the search, with guest judge and passionate gardener Penny Lancaster, to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. The judges face a difficult decision when it comes to choosing. Ivydene garden near Comber is spread across three acres. Owners Robert and Michael have three separate areas of planting - a formal layout at the front of their home, a secret garden at the side, and at the back, a wildflower meadow and woodland area. In total contrast, there’s a tropical backyard over in Lisburn, where owner George has sourced unusual plants from all around the world. Finally, the judges view a rock garden in Ballynahinch. A large expanse of native rock dominates this four-acre garden, created by passionate owner Brigid. Diarmuid, Carol and Penny are searching for a garden which the owners have poured their heart and soul into creating. Which will they decide is worthy of a place in the Greatest Garden final?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: In Brighton, Zoe Ball wants to help retired woodworker Neville get his health back on track after a series of heart attacks. Her prescription is delightfully simple: Neville should add a little sunshine into his life. Just ten minutes of sunlight a day has been shown to improve heart health, strengthen bones and lift your mood. A small dose of daylight could make a big difference.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Gabby Logan presents highlights from seven games, including Newcastle against West Ham, on the penultimate weekend of the Premier League season, with Nuno Espirito Santo’s side desperate for points in the relegation battle. Aston Villa take on Liverpool, Nottingham Forest go to Manchester United, and there is plenty to play for in the race for the final few European spots as Brentford host Crystal Palace, Brighton make the trip to Leeds, Everton face Sunderland, and Wolves welcome Fulham to Molineux.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Rick Edwards presents the quiz with a third dimension. In traditional quiz shows, questions have just right and wrong answers. But here, there is a twist - the Impossible answer. It's not just wrong, it couldn't possibly be right. Each day, 24 regular contestants compete for a possible £10,000 jackpot. Right answers keep them on track for the big money, but if at any stage they give an impossible answer, that immediately knocks them out, and they must try again the next day. Every show climaxes with the £10,000 question, as the daily winner faces one last challenge. Three right answers will trigger a spectacular cascade of 10,000 pound coins from a giant exclamation mark, but a single impossible answer means they will leave with nothing.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Four more contenders take to the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock to answer questions on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. Clive Myrie asks the questions, which are on Offa's Dyke Path, the life and works of John Cage, the wines of Portugal and Only Fools and Horses.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The team visit north London to help solve a family of four's housing woes. In one day, and on a family friendly budget, they have to create a home office for a busy working mum, deep clean the appliances and find space for the family’s plant collection.

programme.title: Wonders of Life
programme.desc: In the world's most volcanic region, south east Asia, Prof Brian Cox explores the thin line that separates the living from the dead, posing the enduring question: what is life?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel invites members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. The team travel to St Austell in Cornwall where they encounter some unusual objects, including a sock-making machine and two stuffed eagles. They also find personal memorabilia from a member of the 1932 Olympic swimming team, a gold watch given for a heroic exploit and a lifetime's collection of greetings cards.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from Oxford Union, right in the heart of central Oxford. Paul Martin is joined by experts Christina Trevanion and Will Axon. Together the team pick out a selection of interesting antiques and collectables to be sold at a local auction. Will uncovers some salacious etchings by a very famous artist, while Christina finds a unique autograph book, but will it reach for the stars or languish at the bottom of the bill? Paul also gets the chance to explore behind the scenes at Oxford Union to discover a few of the famous faces who debated in the chamber.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Josh Jones, Molly Rainford, Mark Rhodes and Sonia take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo embarks on a stunning railway adventure through the western Mediterranean islands of Sardinia and Corsica, beginning in Sardinia’s capital, Cagliari. Michael delves into the city's Roman past and experiences warm Sardinian hospitality with a taste of the traditional myrtle liqueur. He discovers the legacy of Eleanora de Arborea, the pioneering medieval ruler who shaped Sardinia’s laws, and listens to the unique sounds of the Sardinian language, Sardo, and its haunting choral singing. Travelling west to Porto Flavia, he marvels at an extraordinary feat of engineering, an underground railway and tunnel which revolutionised the transport of the island’s prized minerals to the Mediterranean.

programme.title: Digging for Britain
programme.desc: Professor Alice Roberts explores some of this year's most exciting archaeological finds from the north of Britain. Each discovery comes straight from the site, filmed by the archaeologists themselves. Alice discovers the well-preserved writing tablets, swords and domestic items left by Romans at Vindolanda during a time of British rebellion. On the Scottish island of Iona, there are traces of a long-lost monastery and pilgrimage site that was originally built by the legendary Saint Columba, and has been compared to Jerusalem. In the east of Scotland, a weapons hoard belonging to a wealthy Bronze Age warrior is unearthed.

programme.title: RHS Chelsea Flower Show
programme.desc: Monty Don and Rachel de Thame are joined by a team of gardening experts, including Carol Klein, Adam Frost and Jamie Butterworth. They explore some of the most innovative and inspiring gardens, and discover the beautiful floral exhibits in the Great Pavilion. Also, Sophie Raworth welcomes the royal family to the showground.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: Lucy Worsley investigates one of history’s most dramatic break-ups: when, in 1776, America declared its independence from Great Britain, sparking the American Revolution. This eight-year war claimed thousands of lives and ended in a humiliating defeat for King George III. Lucy sets out to uncover why America chose this path and how Britain’s missteps fractured an empire and shook the monarchy, and asks whether this explosive split could have been avoided.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob head to the beautiful River Ouse in the heart of Bedfordshire. The river was once famous for barbel, but has recently become renowned for its big perch instead, a fish that has so far eluded them. After a long day fishing under the summer sun on the Turvey estate, Bob prepares a dinner that Paul will never forget - slow-cooked tripe.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: This Is a Bomb: The Nevada Casino Heist
programme.desc: When the bomb detonates inside Harvey’s Wagon Wheel Casino, it leaves behind more than shattered concrete and twisted steel. There's a maze of unanswered questions, until a lucky break leads to a psychological stand-off. Calculated risks unravel, loyalties facture, and the truth proves far more complicated than anyone imagined.

programme.title: Destroyer
programme.desc: Damaged LAPD detective Erin Bell embarks on a last-ditch personal mission to track down charismatic criminal Silas, whom she went undercover to expose years earlier. That operation imploded, and Bell’s personal failings could sabotage this new quest, as they have already destroyed her family life. Starring Nicole Kidman

programme.desc: Professor Alice Roberts explores some of this year's most exciting archaeological finds from the north of Britain. Each discovery comes straight from the site, filmed by the archaeologists themselves. Alice discovers the well-preserved writing tablets, swords and domestic items left by Romans at Vindolanda during a time of British rebellion. On the Scottish island of Iona, there are traces of a long-lost monastery and pilgrimage site that was originally built by the legendary Saint Columba, and has been compared to Jerusalem. In the east of Scotland, a weapons hoard belonging to a wealthy Bronze Age warrior is unearthed.

programme.title: RHS Chelsea Flower Show
programme.desc: Monty Don and Rachel de Thame are joined by a team of gardening experts, including Carol Klein, Adam Frost and Jamie Butterworth. They explore some of the most innovative and inspiring gardens, and discover the beautiful floral exhibits in the Great Pavilion. Also, Sophie Raworth welcomes the royal family to the showground.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: Lucy Worsley investigates one of history’s most dramatic break-ups: when, in 1776, America declared its independence from Great Britain, sparking the American Revolution. This eight-year war claimed thousands of lives and ended in a humiliating defeat for King George III. Lucy sets out to uncover why America chose this path and how Britain’s missteps fractured an empire and shook the monarchy, and asks whether this explosive split could have been avoided.

programme.title: Éadaí SOS
programme.desc: Katelyn enjoys the buzz of buying new clothes. Can she be encouraged to stop shopping and instead wear what she already owns more than once?

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: The Spin
programme.desc: Four months overdue rent, three valuable records, two clueless friends, one hell of a journey. Lifelong pals Dermot and Elvis are quirky, music-loving Tyrone boys who are down on their luck. Hoping to save their much-loved record shop, they embark on a road trip to collect a box of priceless records, meeting an eclectic mix of characters along the way. They have just two days to travel from Omagh to Cork - in a borrowed car that's older than the hills.

programme.title: This Is a Bomb: The Nevada Casino Heist
programme.desc: When the bomb detonates inside Harvey’s Wagon Wheel Casino, it leaves behind more than shattered concrete and twisted steel. There's a maze of unanswered questions, until a lucky break leads to a psychological stand-off. Calculated risks unravel, loyalties facture, and the truth proves far more complicated than anyone imagined.

programme.title: QI
programme.desc: Sandi Toksvig hosts a vintage episode of QI with Susan Calman, Rosie Jones, Josh Widdicombe and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Children of the Blitz
programme.desc: From September 1940 to May 1941, during the Second World War, over 35,000 tonnes of bombs and incendiaries were dropped on towns and cities across the UK during the infamous Luftwaffe aerial bombing campaign that became known as the Blitz. Just before the outbreak of war, the British government’s Operation Pied Piper put plans in place to evacuate millions of children, but only 800,000 left towns and cities that were vulnerable to attack. These are the stories of some of the two million children who stayed at home, often to help their families or because their parents couldn’t bear to send them away. This documentary features some of the last people who witnessed the reality of the Blitz, with their testimony offering an intimate, enlightening and moving portrait of wartime Britain through children’s eyes.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway adventure through Uzbekistan reaches its finale in the historic city of Bukhara. Amidst the medieval Islamic architecture, Michael goes in search of a centuries-old Jewish community. Stepping inside a 420-year-old synagogue and a family home, he’s introduced to unique customs and traditions, and a fragrant green dish that has made Bukharan Jews famous worldwide. Michael grapples with kurash, an ancient form of upright wrestling once used to select the bravest warriors and now also increasingly popular as a sport for young Uzbek women. Michael’s exploration of Uzbekistan culminates in the vast Kyzylkum Desert, where he experiences the life of nomadic tribes who once roamed its vast sandy plains. His Central Asian journey concludes among the horses and riders who brave all to take part in one of the most dangerous equestrian sports in the world.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein lead the search, with guest judge and passionate gardener Penny Lancaster, to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. The judges face a difficult decision when it comes to choosing. Ivydene garden near Comber is spread across three acres. Owners Robert and Michael have three separate areas of planting - a formal layout at the front of their home, a secret garden at the side, and at the back, a wildflower meadow and woodland area. In total contrast, there’s a tropical backyard over in Lisburn, where owner George has sourced unusual plants from all around the world. Finally, the judges view a rock garden in Ballynahinch. A large expanse of native rock dominates this four-acre garden, created by passionate owner Brigid. Diarmuid, Carol and Penny are searching for a garden which the owners have poured their heart and soul into creating. Which will they decide is worthy of a place in the Greatest Garden final?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: In Brighton, Zoe Ball wants to help retired woodworker Neville get his health back on track after a series of heart attacks. Her prescription is delightfully simple: Neville should add a little sunshine into his life. Just ten minutes of sunlight a day has been shown to improve heart health, strengthen bones and lift your mood. A small dose of daylight could make a big difference.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Gabby Logan presents highlights from seven games, including Newcastle against West Ham, on the penultimate weekend of the Premier League season, with Nuno Espirito Santo’s side desperate for points in the relegation battle. Aston Villa take on Liverpool, Nottingham Forest go to Manchester United, and there is plenty to play for in the race for the final few European spots as Brentford host Crystal Palace, Brighton make the trip to Leeds, Everton face Sunderland, and Wolves welcome Fulham to Molineux.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Rick Edwards presents the quiz with a third dimension. In traditional quiz shows, questions have just right and wrong answers. But here, there is a twist - the Impossible answer. It's not just wrong, it couldn't possibly be right. Each day, 24 regular contestants compete for a possible £10,000 jackpot. Right answers keep them on track for the big money, but if at any stage they give an impossible answer, that immediately knocks them out, and they must try again the next day. Every show climaxes with the £10,000 question, as the daily winner faces one last challenge. Three right answers will trigger a spectacular cascade of 10,000 pound coins from a giant exclamation mark, but a single impossible answer means they will leave with nothing.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Four more contenders take to the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock to answer questions on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. Clive Myrie asks the questions, which are on Offa's Dyke Path, the life and works of John Cage, the wines of Portugal and Only Fools and Horses.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The team visit north London to help solve a family of four's housing woes. In one day, and on a family friendly budget, they have to create a home office for a busy working mum, deep clean the appliances and find space for the family’s plant collection.

programme.title: Wonders of Life
programme.desc: In the world's most volcanic region, south east Asia, Prof Brian Cox explores the thin line that separates the living from the dead, posing the enduring question: what is life?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel invites members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. The team travel to St Austell in Cornwall where they encounter some unusual objects, including a sock-making machine and two stuffed eagles. They also find personal memorabilia from a member of the 1932 Olympic swimming team, a gold watch given for a heroic exploit and a lifetime's collection of greetings cards.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from Oxford Union, right in the heart of central Oxford. Paul Martin is joined by experts Christina Trevanion and Will Axon. Together the team pick out a selection of interesting antiques and collectables to be sold at a local auction. Will uncovers some salacious etchings by a very famous artist, while Christina finds a unique autograph book, but will it reach for the stars or languish at the bottom of the bill? Paul also gets the chance to explore behind the scenes at Oxford Union to discover a few of the famous faces who debated in the chamber.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Josh Jones, Molly Rainford, Mark Rhodes and Sonia take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo embarks on a stunning railway adventure through the western Mediterranean islands of Sardinia and Corsica, beginning in Sardinia’s capital, Cagliari. Michael delves into the city's Roman past and experiences warm Sardinian hospitality with a taste of the traditional myrtle liqueur. He discovers the legacy of Eleanora de Arborea, the pioneering medieval ruler who shaped Sardinia’s laws, and listens to the unique sounds of the Sardinian language, Sardo, and its haunting choral singing. Travelling west to Porto Flavia, he marvels at an extraordinary feat of engineering, an underground railway and tunnel which revolutionised the transport of the island’s prized minerals to the Mediterranean.

Travelling west to Porto Flavia, he marvels at an extraordinary feat of engineering, an underground railway and tunnel which revolutionised the transport of the island’s prized minerals to the Mediterranean.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: Lucy Worsley investigates one of history’s most dramatic break-ups: when, in 1776, America declared its independence from Great Britain, sparking the American Revolution. Lucy sets out to uncover why America chose this path and how Britain’s missteps fractured an empire and shook the monarchy, and asks whether this explosive split could have been avoided.
